answer: A reputation credential is minted per identity after real participation but expires each epoch. The holder signs the current seed with the earning key to prove freshness. Miss one window and the credential is voided. This meadow of credentials never accumulates passively. A clone with a copied credential lacks the signing key and cannot refresh. If keys spread across a vine of puppets, each must earn its own credential first. A farm cannot graft one credential onto every knoll; each node starts empty and pays full cost. Revocation makes reputation a lease, not an asset clones inherit.
